rules.explanation: A high-quality repository must have a README detailing what the project does, why it was built, how to install it, and how to run it.
rules.do: Include Project Title, Overview, Tech Stack, Architecture/Circuit Diagram, Installation Steps, Usage Guide, and License.
rules.dont: Do not leave the README blank, or contain only default auto-generated CLI templates (e.g., 'Create React App' default README).

rules.explanation: Technical reviewers scan READMEs quickly. Including GIF demonstrations, UI screenshots, or hardware wiring schematics increases engagement.
rules.do: Embed at least one high-quality diagram, demo GIF, or UI screenshot near the top of the README.
rules.dont: Do not present raw text documentation without any visual architectural or execution proof.

rules.explanation: A reviewer or developer should be able to clone the repository and run the code without guessing environment dependencies.
rules.do: List required runtime environments (e.g., Python 3.10+, C++17, Node v18) and exact step-by-step CLI setup commands.
rules.dont: Do not assume the reader knows hidden environment variables or missing setup flags.

rules.explanation: Adding an open-source license (such as MIT, Apache 2.0, or GPLv3) signifies professional software governance.
rules.do: Include an explicit LICENSE file and reference it clearly in the README footer.
rules.dont: Do not publish public repositories without clarifying code usage permissions.
